content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Kubernetes 1.37 is scheduled for release on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, according to the [Kubernetes project's official sneak-peek post](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/07/31/kubernetes-v1-37-sneak-peek/), which is corroborated by [Cloudsmith](https://cloudsmith.com/blog/kubernetes-1-37-what-you-need-to-know) and [PerfectScale](https://www.perfectscale.io/blog/kubernetes-v1-37-sneak-peek). The release graduates the long-standing Metrics API to stable, adds a stable KYAML output form...

recommendations: Consider adding cloudsmith.com and perfectscale.io to config/source_allowlist.txt — both are legitimate, reputable technical publications and the allowlist gap is a config-coverage issue, not a reliability problem.

Attribution is granular — nearly every sentence names which of the three sources it draws from, including explicit corroboration language ('independently confirms', 'also confirms') where two or three sources agree.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 source snapshots read in full from disk (gunzip'd .html.gz, sha256 independently recomputed against manifest.json and matched for all three): source-0.html.gz (kubernetes.io official v1.37 sneak-peek, sha256 bbb7d8c0...f97ca3 match), source-1.html.gz (cloudsmith.com, sha256 535eae7f... match), source-2.html.gz (perfectscale.io, sha256 a1fa7244... match). manifest.json suspicious_patterns is null for all three entries — no injection-scan matches to investigate. Spot-verified against raw extracted text: release date Aug 26 2026 (all 3); Metrics API/KEP-5207/'nine years' beta (source-0 'nine years', source-2 'for years'); Kubelet rootless/KEP-2033 + 'extra layer of isolation' quote (source-0) and 'without changing how you use the kubelet day to day' quote (source-2), both verbatim; KYAML/KEP-5295 stable (source-1, source-2); Pod Certificates/KEP-4317 + PodCertificateRequest, ClusterTrustBundles beta (source-1, source-2); HPA tolerance KEP-4951 and the 10% figure (source-2, verbatim 'fixed 10% tolerance across the entire cluster'); DRA device taints KEP-5055 (source-2); ScaledToZero/KEP-2021 (source-2, verbatim 'adds a ScaledToZero status condition'); CBOR #4222 with '8x faster'/'2x faster' encode/decode figures (source-1, verbatim 'up to 8x faster and decoding 2x faster'); ipvs 1.8->1.40->1.43 timeline and nftables kernel 5.13 requirement (source-0, source-1); kubectl run --filename deprecation, Static Pod configMapRef/secretRef fix and PreventStaticPodAPIReferences gate removal, cgroup v1 refusal since 1.35, Volume Health Monitor reset to alpha since a 1.21 attempt (all source-0, corroborated source-2 on Volume Health Monitor); Cloudsmith's 86 total / 28 graduating / 16-to-stable / 34 net-new-alpha enhancement counts and July 21 2026 publication date (source-1, verbatim 'we are seeing 86 enhancements', '28 changes tracked as Graduating', 'just 16 enhancements are graduating to stable', '34 Net New to Alpha enhancements', datePublished 2026-07-21). No hallucinated quotes or misattributions found; every direct quote in the body appears verbatim in its cited snapshot.
editor_notes.selinuxmount_omission_check: The article does not mention SELinuxMount (KEP-1710, 'Speed up recursive SELinux label change') even though all three 1.37 sources cover it prominently: source-0 lists it under 'Breaking changes in Kubernetes v1.37' with the line 'SELinuxMount is expected to reach GA and be enabled by default in v1.37'; source-1 (Cloudsmith) lists '#1710 Speed up recursive SELinux label change / Stage: Graduating to Stable' and notes it was 'rolled out across Kubernetes 1.36 and 1.37 through feature gates'; source-2 (PerfectScale) states 'SELinuxMount graduates to GA and is enabled by default in v1.37.' This appears to be a deliberate omission, since the archive already carries a signed, immutable April 2026 article (src/content/articles/2026-04/21-kubernetes-v136-arrives-with-security-hardening-selinux-acceleration-and-expanded-ai-hardware-support.md) whose summary states SELinux volume labelling 'reached GA' in v1.36, sourced from the March 30 2026 v1.36 sneak-peek. I independently re-verified that April claim against its own archived snapshot (sources/2026-04/kubernetes-v136-.../source-0.html.gz, sha256 fbd9ab94... matches manifest) rather than trusting the bot's stated reasoning: the March 2026 v1.36 sneak-peek does say, verbatim, 'Now in v1.36, it reaches stable and defaults to all volumes, with Pods or CSIDrivers opting in via spec.SELinuxMount' under 'Featured enhancements of Kubernetes v1.36' — so the April article accurately reported what Kubernetes' own pre-release forecast said at the time. The discrepancy is therefore real, not a bot sourcing error on either side: the v1.36 sneak-peek forecast full GA/default-on for this KEP in v1.36, but the current v1.37 sneak-peek instead lists the SAME KEP-1710 under 1.37's 'Breaking changes' as only now (in 1.37) reaching GA and being enabled by default — meaning the feature's default-on rollout evidently slipped a release between the March forecast and what actually shipped, a common occurrence for Kubernetes sneak-peeks, which explicitly disclaim 'This is not a commitment and the release content is subject to change.' Given that reconciling this nuance accurately would require language distinguishing 'API GA' from 'enabled-by-default GA' across two releases — and that the published April article cannot be edited — omitting the item from this 1.37 article rather than risking a confusing or seemingly contradictory claim is a defensible, conservative editorial call, not a sign of the bot mishandling or covering up a real discrepancy. It does not misstate anything (omission of one feature among many is a legitimate scope choice, not a factual error), so it does not warrant a correction or rejection. Flagging here for the record in case a future editor wants to publish a standalone note reconciling the two articles.
